newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cenbank closes two small banks, brokerages.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cenbank closes two small banks, brokerages.

text.p: Brazil's Central Bank closed two small banks and two brokerages on Friday for alleged irregularities in the dealing of various types of public fixed income securities, Central Bank President Gustavo Loyola said.
"These institutions used to buy and sell public titles way out of line with market value and charge unreasonable commissions," Loyola charged at a news conference.

Loyola said authorities shut down banks Banco Maxi-Divisa S.A. and Banco Vetor SA and brokerage houses Perfil Corretora de Cambio, Titulos e Valores Mobiliarios Ltd and Vetor Corretora de Valores e Cambio SA.
In addition, he said the bank has liquidated 10 small investment houses that work with brokerages to carry out securities operations.
All of the institutions involved were participating in activities which may have facilitated money laundering, Loyola charged.

Some of the institutions were also involved in an ongoing investigation into an alleged multi-million dollar fraud scheme involving state and municipal bonds, Loyola said, refusing to name any of the institutions.
